answer: Bonded escrow makes each identity costly to operate: when evidence links k identities to coordinated equivocation, the protocol applies a penalty proportional to k², not k, capturing their shared attack. Detection also triggers an exponential capital-loss multiplier, so a sybil swarm risks far more than its linear stake; asymmetric depreciation compounds the cost. Even a tundra store of timber or nectar cannot make that exposure disappear.
